questions.question: When should drivers obey posted speed limits?

options.text: Only when police officers are present

questions.explanation: Always obey posted speed limits. Check your speedometer often to make sure you are driving within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When should you fasten your safety belt?
questions.explanation: Fasten your safety belt before the engine is started. The law requires drivers to wear seat belts while driving.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do before turning?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must have the right-of-way at all times. Always let them cross before you proceed.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red traffic light. Also obey all orders from police officers directing traffic, regardless of traffic signs or signals.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you must stop until they are completely clear of your path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: At intersections with stop signs on all four corners, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: All drivers should offer to let other cars go first.

questions.explanation: At intersections with stop signs on all corners, vehicles should go in the order they arrived. Come to a complete stop and let any vehicle that arrived before you go first.

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly jump or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so more may be nearby but out of sight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists cannot use turn signals. Instead, they use hand and arm signals. When a bicyclist holds their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Allow extra space for drivers to merge safely into traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Allow extra space for drivers to merge safely into traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will be merging into your lane. Check your mirrors and side, then move to another lane if you can, so merging drivers have a clear path.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Before moving your vehicle, also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure items inside and on your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They reduce reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Check for vehicles in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles go first, no matter when they arrive.
Look in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop. Look in all directions for traffic before you proceed.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking caffeine, or other actions cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Orange-colored signs mean:
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped, orange, and have black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce tire grip. You should slow down to maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, lowers concentration, slows your reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they cross illegally, you must stop for them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits turns in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked line and only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Honk to alert them to your presence.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog must always be given the right-of-way. They have absolute priority.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no safety barrier, you should:

options.text: Assume trains do not usually cross there.
Look both ways for trains before crossing.
Cross quickly if you think you can beat the train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways for trains before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look both ways for oncoming trains before crossing. If a train is coming, stop at a safe distance and wait. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to the car ahead):

options.text: Cannot result in a traffic ticket.

questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can lead to aggressive driving. You may receive a traffic ticket for driving unsafely.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:

options.text: Play loud music while driving to distract yourself.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to release your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving ability. If you are angry, upset, afraid, or worried, take time to calm down before driving. You need to focus completely on the road.
